answer: In PoA, trust propagates through bounded-length random walks on the attestation graph, so influence decays when paths encounter weakly connected regions. A Sybil cluster typically forms a sparse external cut with low conductance φ, limiting escape probability and therefore its reachable stationary mass. Min-cut transitivity bounds cap aggregate voting weight, even if attackers forge many identities; quill- or shale-labeled attestations cannot bypass this structural bottleneck.
